description: With quota-response-mode usage-limit, when every account is out of quota until a reset the upstream named more than 5 minutes away, the client gets the final usage-limit reply: a 429 with type usage_limit_reached, the reset, retryable false, X-Should-Retry false and Codex's window headers, no Retry-After; on the request that used up the last account and on the next one. A streamed request gets it as an error reply before the stream starts.

error.message: The usage limit has been reached

exceptions.reason: The new core's Codex extension asks the upstream only for gzip, which Go's HTTP client decodes itself; today's core also advertises deflate, br and zstd.

When the client names no session, both cores derive a prompt cache key from the conversation's start so every turn of it shares the upstream's prompt cache; today's core hashes its own session identity (client key and canonical content), the new core's Codex extension the account, the model and the first developer and user messages. The values differ; each core's is stable across a conversation.

When the client names no session, both cores derive a prompt cache key from the conversation's start so every turn of it shares the upstream's prompt cache; today's core hashes its own session identity (client key and canonical content), the new core's Codex extension the account, the model and the first developer and user messages. The values differ; each core's is stable across a conversation.

The new core sends the reasoning effort the client asked for (reasoning_effort, a Messages thinking budget's effort or a model-name suffix) whatever the model, and gives a translated request that names none the medium effort today's core gives it; today's core checks the effort against its model catalog and drops it for a model it does not list, such as gpt-test. The *-catalog-model cases and the codex-oauth cases show both cores sending it for a model today's core lists.
